clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within the next three years: your late nights and withdrawal from activities; your move to conservatory and fusion with Rafe; your wrist injury that stopped your playing; conflict with Rafe; absorption in fixing radios; your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery; and your low functioning and anxiety through the community college year. Your father came back into the family that January after years away, and you and your mother moved through rentals and rebuilds on Quarry Lane and Hollin Road, all within these months. Your stung feeling about your father not knowing of your film sits here too, alongside your growing drive again. Every shift in these months is yours and your family's reactions passing between you, as your footing shifted with your grandfather gone, your mother remarrying, and your own playing ended by injury.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008

Two shifts count—your distance from your mother and your conflict with her—held together by her death and your move away, and the silence held until you settled into the nursing programme. This is your own period with your mother; no one else's shifts show in these months.
